entries.For the people of Dwarven Doors the choi: For the people of Dwarven Doors the choice was stark: either drudge as downtrodden slaves for the orcs until the end of their brief and miserable lives, or risk all for freedom and rise against their cruel overlords. Little did they suspect that their struggle would be the hinge of great events that might restore the Northlands to the glory they had once known.
entries.At first, the incursions were mere rabbl: At first, the incursions were mere rabble that were easily felled. Complacent in their own prowess, the people of the Dwarven Doors ignored the orcs even as the raids grew more numerous and threatening. With time, the raiding parties grew into war bands; then at last, there arose a mighty warlord of the Bloody Sword tribe, Khazg Black-Tusk, who surrounded the entirety of their defences with a great host of warriors.
entries.It was a time of doom and great deeds, o: It was a time of doom and great deeds, of fire and blood and slaughter. The men and dwarves fought valiantly. But there were always, it seemed, more orcs to replace the slain, while the defenders could find no succour. Pleas for help went unheeded in other lands for men, elves, and even dwarves, were wrapped up in their own affairs and struggles or deemed the orcs too far away to bring unto them harm.
entries.After a year and a day of grim battle, t: After a year and a day of grim battle, the city fell. The streets of the Dwarven Doors ran with gore. The dwarves retreated into the caverns Knalga, but the humans who survived were enslaved. Cut off from contact with the surface, the dwarves of Knalga fought on, but knew their subjugation could not be averted for ever.
entries.Dark years passed; human generations gre: Dark years passed; human generations grew up and died in slavery, and with every passing year came closer to forgetting that their ancestors had ever been free. They might have completely forgotten were it not for a fateful day. The day that changed the lives of the people of Dwarven Doors — for ever.
entries.He came charging out of the woods, his c: He came charging out of the woods, his cape streaming in the breeze, his sword flashing quicker than thought. All around him, the hated orcs fell. To his right fought an elderly mage whose deep voice boomed incantations over the clamour of the battle. To his left, glowing with faerie fire, was a great lord of the elves. They were followed closely by a small but powerful elvish army.
As quickly as it had begun, it was over. Konrad reached the entrance to the tunnels and ushered his men through. Then he turned one last time to face the peasants. Raising his sword in salute and farewell, he called out to them: ‘Hold fast your hope, for one day you shall be free!’ Then he was gone.
entries.Then one day Al’Tar, the current ‘master: Then one day Al’Tar, the current ‘master’ of Dwarven Doors, was attacked by a neighbouring tribe of orcs. Tallin seized his moment. Using knowledge born of years of watching, listening, and planning, he managed to steal a few weapons and a small amount of Al’Tar’s gold. He fled to an abandoned ruin in the forest to rally his fellow peasants.
entries.Brave words, Tallin, but if I didn’t kno: Brave words, Tallin, but if I didn’t know you better I’d say you were moon-touched. These are not weapons, just pitchforks and hunting bows. We have no armour, no training. Are we supposed to beat them with bad breath and colourful language?
entries.But, but, but... Are you full of nothing: But, but, but... Are you full of nothing but doubts? (Sigh) Yes, it will be a massacre. But would you rather live as slaves to the orcs for ever?
entries.You dare greatly, you miserable excuse f: You dare greatly, you miserable excuse for an orc! How dare you step on to my land!
entries.The war council’s thoughts quickly turne: The war council’s thoughts quickly turned to the dwarves, close allies in the past. However, nobody knew the state of things in the Knalgan tunnels. The bravest of scouts found in there the spoor of many trolls, and of even viler creatures. For years rumours had spread of the dwarves, slain during the invasion of Knalga, now risen in unlife to roam the tunnels. To Tallin and the others, fighting through all manner of unknown monsters in the mere hope of finding surviving dwarves held but little appeal.
entries.So the matter lay. The peasants dithered: So the matter lay. The peasants dithered from one suggested plan of action to the next, never arriving at any conclusion. However, some unlooked help arrived in the form of a small band of woodsrunners — escapees from the orcs, grown wood-wise and crafty, and in contact with larger bands of poachers and outlaws roaming the night. Embassies were sent; agreements made. A handful of experienced fighters, scarred and close-mouthed, came to Dwarven Doors to find and train the willing in their rugged fighting style.
entries.Move Tallin to the dwarvish area to meet: Move Tallin to the dwarvish area to meet Lord Hamel
entries.By frying every orc, troll or skeleton I: By frying every orc, troll or skeleton I come across. Duh! Those monsters desecrated my life’s work, now I shall not rest till I send every last one of them to hell! Oh, and just between me and you, it is actually good fun — more fun, anyway, than sitting on your backside studying all day...
entries.Hordes of trolls and skeletons! Where?!: Hordes of trolls and skeletons! Where?! Let’s go and burn ’em all!
entries.whisper^Is it safe to have this lunatic: Is it safe to have this lunatic with us?
entries.Hey look, it’s an ancient gate. It seems: Hey look, it’s an ancient gate. It seems the trolls were too stupid to work out how to open it.
entries.Another gate... I guess I’ll kick it dow: Another gate... I suppose I’ll kick it down like the other one.
entries.We are in a dire situation indeed — but: We are in a dire situation indeed — but just see — the trolls and the skeletons are also attacking each other. We must all stay together in one group; let each man support the man next to him. If our ranks are imposing enough the monsters may shy away from us in favour of easier prey.
entries.Good, there are no more monsters lurking: Good, there are no more monsters lurking in these parts of the tunnels. I think I can hear the clamour of dwarves just ahead. Come on men, let’s go and meet them.
entries.Yes, that touches on the main reason for: Yes, that touches on the main reason for our visit. We have broken free, but to stay free we need better weapons and armour. Clubs and pitchforks will not carry us through the long run.
entries.Dwarves are known to be the finest metal: Dwarves are known to be the finest metalworkers and weaponsmiths. We were hoping that you would be able to help us.
entries.Aye, our craft is great... but we dinna’: Aye, our craft is great... but we dinna’ ha’ much of weapons and armour ourselves. We’re but a remnant that survived the orcs’ in-taking of these caves. There may be other remnants; but if there are, we dinna’ yet ken of them.
entries.Oh, there are orcs enough down here, but: Oh, there are orcs enough down here, but ye’ll not likely see them; they hide from us like vermin. You see, lad, in these caves there is no more fearsome a foe than a dwarf. Not only do we move through the caves swiftly, but we know them like the backs of our hands. All those years ago, the orcs did indeed manage to swamp our defences with their sheer numbers, but not before we surprised and slew their leader — that cursed Khazg Black-Tusk! Since then, although the orcs still foul these caves with their stench, their attacks have been unco-ordinated and erratic, wi’ the orcs as likely to attack each other as they are to attack us.
entries.With all respect, my Lord Hamel, we the: With all respect, my Lord Hamel, we the people from Dwarven Doors have faced certain death many times now. Rising against the orcs was said to be certain death. Plunging headfirst into these bleak caves was said to be certain death. If that is our fate, so be it. Until that time comes, I will lead my people to fight for our freedom!
entries.Och, human though ye be, ye speak very l: Och, human though ye be, ye speak very like a dwarf, lad. Form up, men! To the mines! Let the guardsmen stay behind along with the non-combatants — for their safety and to hold the keep.
entries.Ahahahaha! Yes, smash the skeletons! Sma: A ha ha ha ha! Yes, smash the skeletons! Smash them!
Argh! They are stronger than we thought. Someone go and tell the Master...
entries.What’s with this ‘Master’ business? It’s: What is this ‘Master’ business? It’s starting to make me nervous.
entries.Hey, there goes our lunch! Hmmm, they ar: Hey, there goes our lunch! Hmmm, they are stronger than we thought, let’s go and tell Master.
entries.What’s with this whole ‘Master’ business: What is this whole ‘Master’ business? It’s starting to make me nervous.
entries.HAHAHAHA! Your petty temper tantrums are: HA HA HA HA! Your petty temper tantrums are most amusing, you puny dwarf. Soon I will finish the slaughter that the orcs have begun so promisingly, and Knalga will be all mine! From there I will sweep the whole north of all living creatures, and then swoop down upon Wesnoth!
entries.HAHAHAHA! Such vast threats from one so: HA HA HA HA! Such vast threats from one so small? HA HA HA!
entries.Tallin! Get hold of yourself!: Tallin! Get a hold of yourself!
entries.HAHAHA, you puny weaklings think you can: HA HA HA, you puny weaklings think you can destroy me? Fools! You will all soon be serving me!
entries.But I’m sore vexed. We need better weapo: But I’m sorely vexed. We need better weapons. Luck and spirit can carry us only so far.
entries.There he goes! Quick, get him!: There he goes! Quickly, after him!
entries.Finally! I am free. Lord Tallin, I am fo: Finally! I am free. Lord Tallin, I am for ever in your debt! We will follow you to the end of the world if need be.
entries.It’s just ‘Tallin’, no ‘Lord’. And no pr: It’s just ‘Tallin’, no ‘Lord’. And it was no problem.
entries.If you have no objection, Tallin, we wou: If you have no objection, Tallin, we would like to join you. These Northlands are hardly safe these days for anyone to be travelling on their own, and we could lend valuable help to your cause.
entries.Wow! That’s incredible. Now I understand: Wow! That’s incredible. Now I understand why the bag of bones kept you in gaol; he just simply couldn’t kill you!
entries.Just Tallin, I am no lord. And you are l: Just Tallin, I am no lord. But you are looking better already.
Hey big guy. We aren’t gonna hurt you. We wanna be your friends.
entries.This is the Great Rod of Justice, my boy: This is the Great Rod of Justice, my boy. It was an ancient artefact even when I was young. They say it was crafted by the Great Gods themselves, and given to the first true Ruler of Men to ensure peace, harmony and above all — justice. For hundreds of years it did just that, for during the time it was wielded, the ruling class never became corrupt, the people never lacked justice, and neither evil nor wars troubled the land.
entries.This thing is... incredible! What is suc: This thing is... incredible! What is such a powerful artefact doing hidden all the way back here?
entries.I don’t think there is a person alive wh: I don’t think there is a person alive who knows anything more solid than rumours and legends. There are very few people who even knows it exists!
entries.Some of the most ancient elvish legends: Some of the most ancient elvish legends make some vague mention of this artefact. But beyond that...
entries.Interesting. I wonder who — or what — co: Interesting. I wonder who — or what — could have created such a powerful artefact. There must be one heck of a story behind this thing.
entries.We were originally prisoners of Malifor,: We were originally prisoners of Malifor, but we tunnelled out and escaped. Since then, we have eked out a precarious survival on what we have been able to steal or raid from Malifor.
entries.Gee, what’s with these bodies floating a: Gee, what are these bodies floating around? Is this river some sort of body disposal?
entries.Hold it, people, there’s something just: Hold it, everyone, there’s something just ahead!
Ahh, shut up. Let’s go and kill them.
entries.HAHAHAHA, THAT WEAPON CANNOT HARM ME!: HA HA HA HA, THAT WEAPON CANNOT HARM ME!
entries.HAHAHAHA, YOUR IDIOCY AMUSES ME GREATLY!: HA HA HA HA, YOUR IDIOCY AMUSES ME GREATLY!
entries.HAHAHAHA, FOOL! THE COLD IS MY DOMAIN!: HA HA HA HA, FOOL! THE COLD IS MY DOMAIN!
entries.As they approached they were met with a: As they approached they were met with a most welcome sight: new fortifications, looking very much like the legendary impenetrable dwarvish defences of old, had sprung up everywhere. All of them were manned by alert and well-armed dwarves who hailed them boisterously. Smoke belched from furiously working forges and the heat from the smelters was nearly staggering. New weapons and armour for humans and dwarves alike lay neatly stacked, and the deafening clang of hammers and picks from the dwarves promised more.
entries.Great! How about the weapons and armor?: Great! How about the weapons and armour?
I would be honoured, Lord Hamel.
entries.The humans rested for many days while th: The humans rested for many days while they were equipped with new arms and armour and trained by the dwarves.
entries.Pah! I would like to see those cowardly: Pah! I would like to see those cowardly dwarves try their treachery on me as they did on the Black-Tusk! In any case, those dwarves will soon be grovelling at my feet and equipping my people with the finest weapons. With the dwarvish weapons, and the wealth of Knalga, nothing will be able to stop us. Even that little backwater that you humans call Wesnoth will be nothing but a burnt out, pillaged wreck before long.
entries.So! Your forces are managing to advance: So! Your forces are managing to advance upon me? Very impressive, but it shall do you no good. KNIGHTS!!!
entries.HAHAHA! GOT YOU, SUCKERS!: HA HA HA! GOT YOU, FOOLS!
entries.You are so dead, you human vermin!: You are dead, you human vermin!
entries.I agree, Tallin, it is pointless to carr: I agree, Tallin, it is pointless to cary on.
entries.The dwarves were more than ready for the: The dwarves were more than ready for them, however, and as soon as the humans got through the defences the well-prepared dwarves fell on the battle-weary and bloodied orcs.
entries.Wave after wave of orcs crashed onto the: Wave after wave of orcs crashed on to the dwarven defences only to be shattered.
entries.So you withdrew. Rightly done, me lad. O: So you withdrew. Rightly done, me lad. Our prepared defences will be able to hold the orcs off far longer and with less loss than ye could ha’ done in the open field. I see that my training of you hasna’ been for nought.
entries.Tallin, before I was captured by Malifor: Tallin, before I was captured by Malfor, I used to be in contact with a powerful magician called Ro’Arthian and his brother Ro’Sothian.
entries.Hrmph. These are desperate times. If tho: Hrmph. These are desperate times. If those lunatics of mages will agree to help, I suppose we’ll nae have any other choice but to accept.
entries.Ye’ll need to travel light to reach High: Ye’ll need to travel lightly to reach Highbrook Pass before the orcs mount another assault in force. I think ye should take as little gold as possible. We’ll store the rest in the tunnels furthest away from the attacking orcs in case they break through.
entries.whisper^Duh! His brother Ro’Arthian is t: Duh! His brother Ro’Arthian is the one who taught me magic!
entries.Ro’Arthian, listen to me. We don’t want: Ro’Arthian, listen to me. We don’t want to fight you, we have come here to seek your assistance.
entries.Put Ro’Sothian into that jail over there: Put Ro’Sothian into that gaol over there until we capture his brother.
entries.Come on, guys, it will be great! Those o: Come on, guys, it will be great! Those orcs will never know what hit them! Together we’ll rip them to shreds! If you are planning to retire after this, this is the perfect chance for you two to go out with a bang! You guys will become legends! ‘The two terrible mages, risen from the dead to devastate the orcish hordes!’
entries.Very well, Tallin. We accept under the t: Very well, Tallin. We accept under the terms that your people will for ever leave us in peace after this.
entries.Farewell, my friends. I now go to join m: Farewell, my friends. I now go to join my fallen brothers.
entries.The lich-mages sent forth gryphons to sc: The lich-mages sent forth gryphons to scout the number, formation and deployment of the orcish forces, and to seek allies as well.
entries.Before the humans and dwarves could resp: Before the humans and dwarves could respond to this message, another gryphon arrived with the news that the orcs were holding an elvish sorceress prisoner in the castle of Bitterhold, less than a day’s march to the north-west. The castle had attracted notice because it had been recently rebuilt and manned by a force known to include some of the hardiest and toughest of veteran orcs.
entries.Hah! Yer brain has rotted awa’ entire. T: Hah! Yer brain has rotted awa’ entirely. Think on it, skull-head, what would happen if the elves dinna’ fight and pay the ransom instead?
entries.Well, suppose we do join up with the elv: Well, suppose we do join the elves — assuming they will let us — and we make a combined raid on the fortress, what will the orcs most likely do when the ransom slips from their grasp?
entries.But it would be unwise to trust that the: But it would be unwise to trust that the orcs will stay stupid for ever. If we do go ahead with this raid, we will have to be in and out like lightning.
entries.Elves are deeply honor-bound, especially: Elves are deeply honour-bound, especially in matters that touch their kin. If we rescue the princess, I am certain the deed will not go without reward.
entries.You will win this scenario immediately u: You will win this scenario immediately upon moving on to the hex containing the Princess’s cage.
entries.Are we here to sight-see or to rescue th: Are we here to sight-see or to rescue this blasted sorceress? If you really want to sight-see, then check that orcish encampment south of us.
entries.(<i>hushed</i>) Thank you, my saviors. W: (hushed) Thank you, my saviours. Who has come to rescue me from vile captivity?
entries.Yes, I was afraid that would be your con: Yes, I was afraid that would be your conclusion. What actually happened was that I was captured by an old bone-bag of a lich.
entries.Then they scrounged up bows and cudgels: Then they scrounged bows and cudgels from the dead orcs, and marched into the caves and broke the dwarves out from their encirclement by the undead and trolls.
entries.My lady, we are not seeking to do busine: My lady, we are not seeking to do business here: ‘I do this for you, and you do this for me.’ No, we seek to build everlasting friendships which will forever ensure the peace and prosperity of these Northlands. Therefore, let there be no talk of debts and repayments between us.
entries.Frankly, my lady, I am disappointed. I w: Frankly, my lady, I am disappointed. I was always under the impression that elves were an honourable lot who took their debts seriously.
That is your concern not mine, human.
entries.I can see the dwarvish defenses just ahe: I can see the dwarvish defences just ahead. Let’s go!
entries.Puzzled by the presence of trolls so clo: Puzzled by the presence of trolls so close to the dwarvish defences, the party quickly made their way back to Knalga.
entries.Such a massive and fierce assault it was: Such a massive and fierce assault it was that we had to call upon all our reserves. When that proved insufficient, we had nae other choice then to call some dwarves off the other defences.
entries.It was a ploy. Nae sooner than we ha’ th: It was a ploy. Nae sooner than we ha’ thinned the ranks of the northern defenders, a small force of trolls smashed through the defences and made their way straight for your gold.
entries.Och, we tried, Tallin, but with the orcs: Och, we tried, Tallin, but with the orcs still pressing our southern defences and trolls trying to break through everywhere, we simply ha’ not the power.
entries.I will send another message to them aski: I will send another message to them asking them to send scouts to locate the trolls who took your gold. Mayhap the elves will be able to get between the trolls and their allies.
entries.All right, let’s move out, people!: All right, let’s move out, everyone!
entries.Haha, suckers! We got you now!: Ha ha, suckers! We got you now!
Ha ha ha! They walked right into our trap.
entries.Haha! Look at them run!: Ha ha! Look at them run!
entries.You better get lost, elf, before we kill: You better get lost, elf before we kill you.
entries.This insult will forever be remembered b: This insult will for ever be remembered by the Northern Elves! The day will soon come when your race shall regret your folly!
entries.Hidel, let me introduce to you my savior: Hidel, let me introduce to you my saviour: Tallin.
It is an honour to meet you, Tallin.
entries.I am honored, sir, and I hope that I wil: I am honoured, sir, and I hope that I will live up to the trust that the Northern Elves have bestowed upon me.
entries.Yes, or so I have heard. You honor me, b: Yes, or so I have heard. You honour me, but this brave man reached the mark before you.
entries.Very well, people. The road ahead is cle: Very well, everyone. The road ahead is clear, onwards to victory!
entries.I was not idle in my captivity; I watche: I was not idle in my captivity; I watched, and listened, and learned. The hints I got from my guards’ boastings and foul jests have been confirmed by our scouts; Angthurim is the linchpin of their entire eastern flank. If we could take it, their defence would be near to collapse.
entries.Fitting. My gryphons tell me Angthurim i: Fitting. My gryphons tell me Angthurim is the keystone of their entire eastern flank. If we can destroy it their defence will be near to collapse.
entries.Hahahaha! Very g—: Ha ha ha ha! Very g—
entries.Very well. Forward! Victory or death!: Very well. Forwards! Victory or death!
entries.We have torn the heart from their easter: We have torn the heart from their eastern defences.
entries.Orcs are heavy-footed creatures; Rakshas: Orcs are heavy-footed creatures; Rakshas’ trail was readily followed. But an ominous silence, broken only by the cawing of ravens, brooded over the road he had taken.
entries.Soon they encountered the wrack of a gre: Soon they encountered the wrack of a great battle. Bodies of elves and orcs lay everywhere. Broken weapons and smashed armour were strewn about and elvish arrows and orcish bolts bristled from the nearby trees. The ground was red with blood.
entries.Scattered around him were the bodies of: Scattered around him were the bodies of at least three orcish warlords, and nearly a score of grunts, warriors and crossbowmen. His weapons were notched and broken; his armour dented and smashed. It was clear that his fall had been a battle of valour and glory, worthy to be remembered in the songs of all the kindred races until the end of days.
entries.Now... uphold the honor... of the Northe: Now... uphold the honour... of the Northern... Elves... Recover... the gold... slay this monster... and bring peace... to the... Northlands... Tallin?
entries.At these words, Eryssa arose and wiped a: At these words, Eryssa arose and wiped away her tears. She took command of the surviving elvish forces, for all knew she was a princess of high rank and looked to Hidel’s ward as their leader. Scarcely a face among them was less grim than her own as they took arms and started down Rakshas’ trail.
entries.Hidel... died a hero’s death, one worthy: Hidel... died a hero’s death, one worthy to be sung for ever.
entries.Haha! We got the gold now!: Ha ha! We got the gold now!
entries.Hahaha! Mission accomplished! I’ll send: Ha ha ha! Mission accomplished! I’ll send a wolf to the Master to deliver the gold. Now let’s crush the rest of this scum!
entries.The party once again took up Rakshas’s t: The party once again took up Rakshas’ trail. They soon received a report from a scouting gryphon that in an enormous fortress a few leagues west from them, Rakshas was assembling a massive orcish force, clearly intending to crush their revolt once and for all.
entries.Battle plans were quickly made; the part: Battle plans were quickly made; the party split into three groups. Two of the groups immediately set off north-west and south-west respectively while the third group rested for an hour and then set off west.
entries.Hahahahah! You fools, do you not see tha: Ha ha ha ha ha! You fools, do you not see that you are in the heart of orcish territory? You’ve surrounded yourselves! Why, at this very moment my entire western army is marching this way. They will soon be here and will scatter your forces like chaff!
entries.It’s called ‘The End’, foul orc. Forward: It’s called ‘The End’, foul orc. Forwards! FOR KNALGA!!
entries.The orcs are exceedingly numerous and wa: The orcs are exceedingly numerous and warlike. While they squabble among themselves, their warlike nature turns upon itself, and they are no threat; but when a strong warlord like Rakshas arises among them, their battle-lust becomes a plague upon their neighbours.
entries.Rising to his feet, Hamel raised his han: Rising to his feet, Hamel raised his hands and waited for the clamour to die down.
entries.I thank everyone for the love and honor: I thank everyone for the love and honour bestowed upon me. In honour of that love I accept this responsibility.
entries.Gladly, Tallin. We will stand with the W: Gladly, Tallin. We will stand with the Warders till the end of time if need be.
entries.Tallin, as you know, I have been separat: Tallin, as you know, I have been separated from my race and kinsmen — well, except Eryssa — for many years now. I wish to go back to the elvish forests and live among my kinsmen again. Perhaps I will return some day.
entries.I’m sorry, Tallin, but me and my friends: I’m sorry, Tallin, but my friends and I had better be getting back to our people.
entries.On Father Morvin’s advice, the Council a: On Father Morvin’s advice, the Council approached all the different orcish tribes and made treaties with them. If a chieftain refused to co-operate with the Alliance, he was forcibly removed and a more favourably-disposed leader put in his place.
entries.Thus, from a small, enslaved community,: Thus, from a small, enslaved community, the people of Dwarven Doors — by their fortitude, valour, and wisdom — brought the Northlands out of the darkness and restored them to their former glory.
entries.You wretched monsters! You are going to: You wretched monsters! You will pay for this!
entries.Thera, when this is all over, you should: Thera, when this is all over, you should paint your face and join a theatre.
Which might be sooner then you think.
